record.paper_title: Some open problems in computational algebraic geometry
record.original_question: Determine the algebraic relations among the dihedral invariants on every sublocus of the cyclic moduli of algebraic curves.

evidence.quote: We call such invariants dihedral invariants of hyperelliptic curves.
Problem 17. Determine algebraic relations among "dihedral" invariants for all subloci of the "cyclic" moduli.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. For an integer $g \ge 2$, let $\mathcal{H}_g$ denote the moduli space of hyperelliptic curves of genus $g$. Inside $\mathcal{H}_g$, consider the sublocus $\mathcal{L}_g$ consisting of isomorphism classes of hyperelliptic curves admitting an extra involution (i.e., an involution in the reduced automorphism group other than the identity). A curve in this locus has an affine model of the form
$$y^2 = x^{2g+2} + a_g x^{2g} + a_{g-1} x^{2g-2} + \cdots + a_1 x^2 + 1,$$
on which the dihedral group $D_{2(g+1)}$ acts via $x \mapsto \zeta x$ (for a primitive $(g+1)$-th root of unity $\zeta$) together with $x \mapsto 1/x$. The ring of invariants $k[a_1,\dots,a_g]^{D_{2(g+1)}}$ is generated by certain explicit symmetric polynomials $u_1,\dots,u_m$ in $a_1,\dots,a_g$, called the dihedral invariants; the tuple $(u_1,\dots,u_m)$ generically classifies isomorphism classes of curves in $\mathcal{L}_g$.

More generally, a cyclic curve is a smooth projective curve $C$ admitting a cyclic subgroup $\langle \tau \rangle$ in its automorphism group such that $C / \langle \tau \rangle$ has genus $0$. The cyclic moduli is the locus inside $\mathcal{M}_g$ parametrizing such curves, stratified by signature data of the cyclic cover. On each stratum, one may analogously define dihedral-type invariants associated with the normalizer of $\langle \tau \rangle$ in $\mathrm{Aut}(C)$.

Problem: For every sublocus of the cyclic moduli of algebraic curves, determine explicitly the ideal of algebraic relations satisfied by the corresponding dihedral invariants. That is, for each such stratum, give generators of the relation ideal $I \subset k[U_1,\dots,U_N]$ such that $k[U_1,\dots,U_N]/I$ is the coordinate ring of the image of the stratum under the map given by the dihedral invariants.
artifact.status_search_result: Dihedral invariants of hyperelliptic curves with extra involutions were introduced by Gutierrez and Shaska, who determined the algebraic relations explicitly in low genus (g=2,3,4). Subsequent work on superelliptic and cyclic curves has extended the framework, but a complete determination of the relations among dihedral invariants on every sublocus of the cyclic moduli is not available in the literature; the general problem appears to remain open, with only partial results in special families.

status_evidence.title: Hyperelliptic Curves with Extra Involutions (Gutierrez–Shaska)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces dihedral invariants u_i and computes relations for low genus.
status_evidence.claim: Dihedral invariants and their algebraic relations are determined explicitly in low genus cases.

status_evidence.title: On superelliptic curves of level n and their quotients
status_evidence.snippet: Extends invariant-theoretic framework to superelliptic/cyclic curves with partial results.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations exist for superelliptic curves but full relations on every sublocus of cyclic moduli are not given.

status_evidence.title: The arithmetic of genus two curves
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses moduli and invariants of cyclic covers, leaving general relation problems open.
status_evidence.claim: The general determination of relations on all subloci of cyclic moduli is stated as open.
